QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_10

question.text: Under a Right of First Offer (ROFO), if a selling shareholder receives a LOWER third-party offer than the ROFO-holder's prior offer, the selling shareholder must:

answer.text: Retain the shares — no sale is permitted
Sell at the lower market offer, having exhausted the ROFO-holder's right
Compulsorily sell to the ROFO-holder at the ROFO-holder's previously quoted offer price

explanation.text: The Logic: Under ROFO, the holder gives its best quote FIRST. Then the seller tests the market. If market offers LESS, seller MUST sell to the ROFO-holder at that holder's original quoted price. If market offers MORE, seller is free to sell externally. The Trap: Option A inverts ROFO logic. Retaining shares ignores the mechanism. Renegotiation isn't contractually mandated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this identically. Manager's Pro-Tip: ROFO is founder-friendlier than ROFR — it lets the founder test price discovery without tipping off the market. As Cat II manager, push for ROFR on strategic shareholdings and accept ROFO on promoter-lock-in shares.
